primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Autoimmune synovitis causes symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis with pannus formation, cartilage destruction, and marginal erosions.
vignette: A 42-year-old woman has 6 months of symmetric MCP and PIP pain and swelling with morning stiffness lasting 2 hours. DIP joints are spared.
distractor_notes: Osteoarthritis commonly affects DIP joints and causes shorter morning stiffness.
Psoriatic arthritis often involves DIP joints and may be asymmetric with nail disease.
Gout usually causes acute monoarthritis.
Polymyalgia rheumatica affects shoulder and hip girdles in older adults.
key_expl: Symmetric inflammatory MCP/PIP polyarthritis with prolonged morning stiffness and DIP sparing is classic RA.
objective: Recognize rheumatoid arthritis from joint distribution and inflammatory symptoms.

sources.support: NIAMS describes chronic symmetric inflammatory arthritis affecting small joints.

sources.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes prolonged morning stiffness and joint swelling.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Progressive loss of articular cartilage with subchondral bone remodeling and osteophyte formation causes activity-related pain and brief morning stiffness.
vignette: A 69-year-old woman has knee pain that worsens with walking and improves with rest. Morning stiffness lasts 10 minutes. X-ray shows joint-space narrowing and osteophytes.
lead: Which tissue undergoes the primary degenerative change?
distractor_notes: Synovium may develop secondary inflammation but is not the primary degenerative target.
Muscle weakness can contribute functionally but does not define OA.
Peripheral myelin loss causes neuropathy.
Enthesis disease is characteristic of spondyloarthropathies.
key_expl: Osteoarthritis begins with degeneration of articular cartilage and secondary subchondral remodeling.
objective: Explain the primary tissue pathology of osteoarthritis.

sources.title: Osteoarthritis
sources.support: NIAMS describes degeneration of articular cartilage and joint remodeling in OA.

sources.title: Osteoarthritis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes activity-related joint pain and cartilage loss.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Monosodium urate crystals deposit in joints when urate is supersaturated, causing intense neutrophil-mediated inflammation.
vignette: A 56-year-old man develops abrupt severe pain, erythema, and swelling of the first MTP joint. Synovial fluid shows needle-shaped negatively birefringent crystals.
distractor_notes: Pseudogout has rhomboid weakly positively birefringent calcium pyrophosphate crystals.
Septic arthritis is infectious and lacks the defining urate crystals.
RA is chronic symmetric polyarthritis.
OA is degenerative and noncrystalline.
key_expl: Podagra with needle-shaped negatively birefringent crystals is classic gout.
objective: Recognize gout by joint pattern and crystal morphology.

sources.title: Gout
sources.support: NIAMS describes monosodium urate crystal arthritis and podagra.

sources.title: Gout
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes sudden severe joint pain caused by uric acid crystals.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: T-cell-mediated inflammatory myopathy causes symmetric proximal muscle weakness with elevated muscle enzymes but no characteristic dermatomyositis rash.
vignette: A 52-year-old woman has progressive symmetric proximal muscle weakness and elevated creatine kinase. Skin examination is normal.
correct: Endomysial inflammatory injury of skeletal muscle
distractor_notes: NMJ receptor loss causes myasthenia without CK elevation.
Peripheral demyelination causes neuropathic weakness and sensory/reflex changes.
Dystrophin deficiency presents much earlier in males.
Osteoclast activity affects bone, not muscle.
key_expl: Polymyositis is an inflammatory myopathy with endomysial T-cell-mediated muscle injury.
objective: Differentiate inflammatory myopathy from neuropathic and NMJ causes of weakness.

sources.title: Polymyositis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes inflammatory proximal muscle weakness and elevated muscle enzymes.

sources.title: Inflammatory Myopathies
sources.support: NINDS describes polymyositis and inflammatory muscle injury.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Excessive disorganized osteoclastic resorption followed by compensatory osteoblastic bone formation produces enlarged structurally weak bone and elevated alkaline phosphatase.
vignette: A 72-year-old man has increasing hat size, hearing loss, bone pain, and isolated elevation of alkaline phosphatase with normal calcium.
lead: Which bone-remodeling pattern is most likely?
distractors: Loss of type I collagen synthesis
distractor_notes: Mineralization failure causes osteomalacia.
Osteoclast failure causes osteopetrosis.
Type I collagen defects cause osteogenesis imperfecta.
Paget disease is high-turnover, not low-turnover.
key_expl: Paget disease features accelerated but disorganized resorption and formation.
objective: Explain Paget disease as high-turnover disorganized remodeling.
clues: increased hat size and hearing loss

sources.title: Paget's Disease of Bone
sources.support: NIAMS describes excessive abnormal bone remodeling in Paget disease.

sources.title: Paget disease of bone
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes enlarged bones, hearing loss, and elevated alkaline phosphatase.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Vitamin C is required for hydroxylation of proline and lysine residues in collagen, stabilizing the triple helix; deficiency causes fragile vessels and impaired wound healing.
vignette: A man with severe dietary restriction has bleeding gums, perifollicular hemorrhages, corkscrew hairs, and poor wound healing.
correct: Hydroxylation of proline and lysine in collagen
distractor_notes: Gamma-carboxylation is vitamin K dependent.
Fibrin cross-linking uses factor XIII.
DNA methylation is not the defining vitamin C function.
Hemoglobin glycation is nonenzymatic and unrelated.
key_expl: Ascorbate is required by prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases during collagen synthesis.
objective: Connect scurvy with impaired collagen hydroxylation.
clues: poor wound healing and perifollicular hemorrhage

sources.title: Vitamin C — Health Professional Fact Sheet
sources.support: NIH ODS describes vitamin C as required for collagen hydroxylation.

sources.title: Scurvy
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes bleeding, corkscrew hairs, and poor wound healing from vitamin C deficiency.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Defects in collagen synthesis or processing produce hyperextensible skin, joint hypermobility, easy bruising, and tissue fragility.
vignette: A 21-year-old woman has marked joint hypermobility, hyperextensible skin, easy bruising, and recurrent joint dislocations.
distractor_notes: Marfan syndrome causes tall stature, lens and aortic disease rather than hyperextensible skin.
OI causes fractures and blue sclerae.
Systemic sclerosis causes skin tightening, the opposite phenotype.
Turner syndrome causes short stature and gonadal dysgenesis.
key_expl: Hypermobile joints plus hyperextensible fragile skin strongly suggest Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
objective: Recognize Ehlers-Danlos syndrome from connective-tissue fragility.

sources.title: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes hypermobility, hyperextensible skin, and tissue fragility.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: FBN1 mutations impair fibrillin-rich microfibrils and dysregulate TGF-beta signaling, causing skeletal overgrowth, lens dislocation, and aortic root disease.
vignette: A tall 24-year-old man has arachnodactyly, pectus deformity, superior lens subluxation, and aortic root dilation.
distractor_notes: Type I collagen defects cause OI.
Dystrophin defects cause Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy.
Alpha-1 antitrypsin is an elastase inhibitor but does not cause Marfan syndrome.
Type IV collagen defects cause Alport syndrome.
key_expl: Marfan syndrome is caused by FBN1 variants affecting fibrillin-1.
objective: Associate Marfan syndrome with fibrillin-1 defects.

sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes skeletal, ocular, and aortic manifestations of FBN1 variants.

sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes fibrillin-1 and Marfan syndrome.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Superficial bacterial infection of the epidermis, commonly due to S aureus or group A streptococci, produces fragile vesicles/pustules and honey-colored crusts.
vignette: A 6-year-old child has several superficial facial erosions covered by golden honey-colored crusts after scratching insect bites.
distractor_notes: Cellulitis is a deeper dermal infection with diffuse erythema and warmth.
Herpes zoster causes grouped painful vesicles in a dermatomal distribution.
Tinea corporis causes annular scaly plaques.
Atopic dermatitis is chronic pruritic eczema without classic honey crusts.
key_expl: Superficial erosions with honey-colored crusting are classic nonbullous impetigo.

sources.title: Impetigo
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes superficial bacterial skin infection with honey-colored crusts.

sources.title: About Impetigo
sources.support: CDC describes impetigo and common group A streptococcal involvement.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Bacterial infection of dermis and subcutaneous tissue causes expanding erythema, warmth, edema, and tenderness, commonly from streptococci or S aureus.
vignette: A 58-year-old man develops a tender, warm, expanding erythematous area on the lower leg after a skin fissure. There is no fluctuance or crepitus.
lead: Which tissue compartment is primarily infected?
distractor_notes: Epidermal infection alone is more superficial, as in impetigo.
Fascial infection with disproportionate pain suggests necrotizing fasciitis.
Joint infection causes septic arthritis.
Bone infection is osteomyelitis.
key_expl: Cellulitis is a spreading infection of deeper skin and subcutaneous tissues.
objective: Distinguish cellulitis from superficial and deep necrotizing infection by tissue depth.

sources.title: Cellulitis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes bacterial infection of deeper skin causing warmth, redness, swelling, and pain.

sources.title: About Cellulitis
sources.support: CDC describes cellulitis as bacterial infection of deeper skin tissues.
